Rashi on Niddah 35b:11:1.hebrew: כאן שספרה - בראיותה, בספרה ז' נקיים. מתניתין, דמודו בית שמאי — כשעברו ימי לידה, ועדיין לא ספרה אחריהם שבעה נקיים. והכי קאמר: אף על גב דאמרי בית שמאי ביולדת גרידתא כרוקה וכמימי רגליה, מודים ביולדת בזוב שלא ספרה, דכל זמן שלא ספרה זבה היא; ואם ראתה, לא הוי כרוקה וכמימי רגליה, דאילו רוק מטמא לח ולא יבש, כדאמר בדם הנדה (לקמן נדה נו.): וכי ירוק — כעין רקיקה, דהיינו לח; אבל דמה מטמא לח ויבש, כשאר דם הנדה, כדילפינן בדם הנדה (שם דף נד:):
Rashi on Niddah 35b:11:1.english: Here, where she counted - Regarding her seeing [of blood, in the baraita]: where she counted seven clean days. The mishna, where Beit Shammai concede, [deals with a case] where the days of childbirth passed and she had not yet counted seven clean days after them. And this is what [the mishna] means: Even though Beit Shammai say regarding a standard woman who gave birth [that her blood is] like her spit and her urine, they concede regarding a woman who gave birth as a *zava* who did not count [seven clean days], that as long as she has not counted, she is a *zava*; and if she saw [blood], it is not [merely] like her spit and her urine — for spit imparts impurity [only when] moist and not [when] dry, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] *Dam HaNiddah* (below, Niddah 56a): "And if [the *zav*] spit" [means it must be emitted] in the manner of spitting, which means moist; but her blood imparts impurity [both] moist and dry, like any other menstrual blood, as we derive in [the chapter] *Dam HaNiddah* (there, page 54b).

Rashi on Niddah 35b:12:1.english: And it is taught - [This is read] in an affirmative tone [as a support, not as an objection].

Rashi on Niddah 35b:12:2.hebrew: בית שמאי לשיטתן - כי היכי דמטהרי ביולדת גרידתא, מטהרי בהך, דקסברי: ביומי תלה רחמנא, והא מלו לה כל ימים שלה:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:12:2.english: Beit Shammai follow their opinion - Just as they rule [the blood] pure in [the case of] an ordinary woman who gave birth, they rule [it] pure in this [case], for they hold: The Merciful One made [it] dependent on days, and behold, all of her days have been completed.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:12:3.hebrew: ובית הלל לשיטתן - דקסברי: ביומי וטבילה תלה רחמנא, וכיון דלא טבלה, הוי דמה טמא כטומאת לידה, דהוי אב הטומאה:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:12:3.english: And Beit Hillel follow their opinion - For they hold: The Merciful One made [it] dependent on [both] days and immersion; and since she did not immerse, her blood is impure like the impurity of childbirth, which is a primary source of ritual impurity.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:13:1.english: It is one source - Blood that comes during the days of childbirth and blood that comes during the days of purity come from one source.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:13:2.english: The Torah rendered it impure - All seven [days] for a male and fourteen for a female.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:13:3.english: And the Torah rendered it pure - After that [period].

Rashi on Niddah 35b:14:1.hebrew: נסתם הטמא - לאחר שבועים, ונפתח הטהור:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:14:1.english: The impure is closed - After two weeks, and the pure [source] opens.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:14:2.english: The pure [source] is closed - After eighty [days], and the impure [source] opens.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:16:1.hebrew: לרב רישא - דשופעת מתוך ימי טומאה לימי טהרה, לקולא, וטהורה, ואף על גב דלא פסק, דהא התורה טהרתו:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:16:1.english: According to Rav, the first clause - That [a woman] who continuously discharges from within the days of impurity into the days of purity is [ruled] leniently, and she is pure; and even though [the flow] did not cease, [this is] because the Torah rendered it pure.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:16:2.hebrew: וסיפא - דשפעה מתוך מ' לאחר מ', ומתוך פ' לאחר שמנים, לחומרא, וטמאה לאחר שמנים, דהתורה טמאתו:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:16:2.english: And the latter clause - Where she discharged continuously from within the forty [days] to after the forty, and from within the eighty to after eighty, [is] for stringency; and she is impure after eighty, because the Torah deemed it impure.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:17:1.hebrew: ללוי רישא לחומרא - כיון דלא פסקה, לא נסתם מעין טמא:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:17:1.english: According to Levi, the first clause is to be stringent - Since she did not stop [bleeding], the impure source was not closed.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:17:2.hebrew: וסיפא לקולא - דכיון דלא פסקה, לא נסתם מעין טהור:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:17:2.english: And the latter clause is lenient - For since she did not cease [bleeding], the pure source did not close.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:19:1.hebrew: קס"ד דפסקה - יום או שנים לאחר שבועים. ומשום הכי מטמא לח ויבש, דממעין טמא בא, והתורה לא טהרתו לב"ה אלא ביומי וטבילה:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:19:1.english: It enters your mind that [the discharge] ceased - [And she saw blood] a day or two after the two weeks [of impurity]. And for this reason [the blood] imparts impurity moist and dry, as it comes from an impure source, and the Torah did not purify it, according to Beit Hillel, except through [both] days and immersion.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:19:2.hebrew: אלא ללוי - הא ממעין טהור אתא, דכי פסקה נסתם הטמא:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:19:2.english: But according to Levi - This [blood] comes from the pure source, for when [the discharge] ceased, the impure [source] closed.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:1:1.hebrew: שהוא עושה משכב ומושב - אב הטומאה, מה שאין כן בקרי:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:1:1.english: That he renders bedding and seating - [To be] a primary source of ritual impurity, which is not the case with [one who experienced] a seminal emission.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:20:1.hebrew: בשופעת - מתוך ימי טומאה לימי טהרה, ולא פסקה:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:20:1.english: With [a woman] who discharges continuously - From within the days of impurity into the days of purity, and she did not cease [discharging].

Rashi on Niddah 35b:21:1.english: Granted according to Levi - For he said that according to Beit Hillel, there are two sources.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:21:2.hebrew: היינו דאיכא בין בית שמאי ובית הלל - דלבית הלל שני מעינות הן, וכיון דלא פסק, טמאה, דלא נסתם הטמא. ולבית שמאי מעין אחד הוא, והתורה טהרתו אחר שבועים:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:21:2.english: That is [the difference] between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel - For according to Beit Hillel, they are two sources, and since [the flow] did not cease, she is impure, for the impure [source] was not closed. And according to Beit Shammai, it is one source, and the Torah rendered it pure after two weeks.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:21:3.hebrew: אלא לרב - דאמר מעין אחד הוא, אי בית הלל קיימי כוותיה:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:21:3.english: But according to Rav - Who says that it is one source, if Beit Hillel hold in accordance with him.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:21:4.hebrew: מאי איכא כו' - כלומר, במאי קמיפלגי, ומאי טעמא דבית הלל דמטמאין:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:21:4.english: What is there, etc. - That is to say: In what do they disagree, and what is the reasoning of Beit Hillel who deem [it] impure?

Rashi on Niddah 35b:22:1.hebrew: ביומי וטבילה - לא שנא שופעת, לא שנא פוסקת — כל זמן שלא טבלה, הוי דמה טמא בימי לידתה:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:22:1.english: On days and immersion - It makes no difference whether she discharges continuously or whether she ceases — as long as she has not immersed, her blood is impure during the days of her childbirth.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:23:1.hebrew: ומודים ביולדת בזוב שמטמאה - ואוקימנא כשעברו ימי לידתה ולא ספרה אחריהן ז' נקיים, וקס"ד הכא נמי דפסקה אחר שבועים, ומשום הכי מטמא, דממעיין טמא אתו, והתורה לא טהרתו עד שתשב ז' נקיים כדין זבה:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:23:1.english: And they concede in the case of a woman who gives birth as a zava, that she imparts impurity - And we established [above that the mishna refers to a case] where the days of her childbirth passed and she did not count seven clean days after them. And it enters our minds [to assume] that here too, [the bleeding] ceased after two weeks, and for this reason it imparts impurity [whether moist or dry] — because it comes from an impure source, and the Torah did not purify it until she observes seven clean days, in accordance with the law of a zava.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:24:1.hebrew: אמאי מטמאה - דהא ממקום טהור הוא בא, והרי הוא כדם מגפתה וכרוקה, שמטמא לח משום מעין הזב, ולא יבש:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:24:1.english: Why does she impart impurity - For it comes from a pure place, and it is like the blood of her wound and like her saliva, which imparts impurity [when] moist as a bodily fluid of a zav, and not [when] dry.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:26:1.hebrew: לב"ש אצטריך - דקאמר מעין אחד הוא, ומטהרי לה ביולדת גרידתא אחר ימי לידתה מיד, דביומי תלא רחמנא — אצטריך ביולדת בזוב לאשמועינן דמטמאה:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:26:1.english: It was necessary for Beit Shammai - For since [Beit Shammai] say that it is one source, and they declare her pure in [the case of] an ordinary woman who gave birth immediately after the days of her childbirth, for the Merciful One made [it] dependent on days — it was necessary in [the case of] a woman who gives birth as a *zava* to teach us that she imparts impurity.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:26:2.hebrew: דהני מילי - דהוי דם טוהר לאחר ימי לידה ביולדת גרידתא, אבל ביולדת בזוב, דבעיא ספורים — כל זמן שלא ספרה, הוי דמה כדם זיבה, דהא מחד מעין אתי, ותורה לא טהרתו עד שתספור, כדכתיב: ״ואחר תטהר״ — ״אחר״, אחר לכולן:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:26:2.english: That this statement applies - That [the blood] is blood of purity after the days of childbirth [applies only] in [the case of] a woman who only gave birth; but in [the case of] a woman who gives birth as a zava, who requires counting [seven clean days], as long as she has not counted, her blood is like the blood of ziva, for it comes from one source, and the Torah did not purify it until she counts, as it is written: "And after that she shall be clean" (Leviticus 15:28) — "after": after all of them [have been counted].

Rashi on Niddah 35b:27:1.hebrew: דותה תטמא - קרא יתירא הוא, דה"ל למכתב וטמאה ז' ימים כימי נדה ולשתוק:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:27:1.english: Her menstrual sickness she shall be impure - It is a superfluous phrase, as [the verse] should have written: "And she shall be impure seven days as the days of menstruation," and remained silent.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:28:1.english: To include that she imparts impurity to her sexual partner like a menstruating woman, and to include the nights like the days - So that you should not say: "Days" is written [implying only daytime and not nights].

Rashi on Niddah 35b:28:2.hebrew: משום הכי בעיא - הפסקה שבעה נקיים, דממעין דמים טמאים אתי, והתורה לא טהרתו עד שתספור שבעה נקיים, כדכתיב דותה תטמא:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:28:2.english: It is for this reason that she requires - A cessation of seven clean days, because [the blood] comes from a source of impure blood, and the Torah did not purify it until she counts seven clean days, as it is written: "Her menstrual sickness she shall be impure."

Rashi on Niddah 35b:2:1.hebrew: אלא פשיטא בראייה ראשונה - דהוי בכלל קרי, כדאקשינן לעיל: הזב ואשר תצא ממנו וכו':
Rashi on Niddah 35b:2:1.english: Rather, it is obvious [that it refers to] the first sighting - For it was included in [the category of] a seminal emission, as we objected above: "The zav, and he from whom [a flow of seed] goes out," etc.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:5:1.hebrew: דיהה - כלומר, מתמקמק ונפרד, ואינו קשור:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:5:1.english: Runny - That is to say, it decomposes and separates, and is not cohesive.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:5:2.english: Unfertilized - [An egg] that does not produce a chick under a hen.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:8:1.hebrew: יולדת בזוב תוכיח שאם טבלה - לאחר שמנתה ז' נקיים, לבד ימי טומאת לידה:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:8:1.english: A woman who gives birth as a zava will prove that if she immersed - After she counted seven clean [days], aside from the days of the impurity of childbirth.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:8:2.hebrew: וראתה טהורה היא - דדם טהור הוא, וכי לא טבלה וראתה, טמא:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:8:2.english: And she saw [blood], she is pure - For it is pure blood, and when she did not immerse and saw [blood], it is impure.

Rashi on Niddah 35b:9:1.hebrew: אמרו להם בית שמאי הוא הדין כו' - כלומר, כי היכי דאמרינן ביולדת גמורה גרידא שלא טבלה וראתה — טהורה, כך יולדת בזוב שעברו עליה ימי לידה ושבעה נקיים ולא טבלה וראתה — טהורה:
Rashi on Niddah 35b:9:1.english: Beit Shammai said to them: The same rule applies, etc. - That is to say: Just as we say regarding an ordinary woman who gave birth alone, that [if] she did not immerse and saw [blood], she is pure — so too, [regarding] a woman who gives birth as a *zava*, for whom the days of childbirth and seven clean [days] have passed and she did not immerse and saw [blood], she is pure.

Tosafot on Niddah 35b:15:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו שופעת מתוך שבעה כו' - איכא בינייהו טובא, כל הני דפריך בסמוך; אלא דפשוט יותר נקט:
Tosafot on Niddah 35b:15:1.english: There is [a difference] between them: [a woman who] discharges continuously from within seven, etc. - There are many [differences] between them, [namely] all those [cases] that [the Gemara] challenges nearby; rather, [the Gemara] took [the case that is] simpler.

Tosafot on Niddah 35b:20:1.hebrew: בשופעת - והשתא, אפי' בטבלה יטמאו בית הלל לח ויבש; ומתניתין דנקט ולא טבלה, משום בית שמאי. וא"ת, דבעדיות קתני הך דיולדת גבי קולי בית שמאי וחומרי בית הלל, הלא בשופעת מתוך מ' (למה) הוו בית הלל לקולא? וי"ל, דכי אתשיל, בתחלת לידה אתשיל:
Tosafot on Niddah 35b:20:1.english: [With a woman who is] continuously discharging - And now [that Levi establishes the mishna as dealing with a continuous discharge], even if she had immersed, Beit Hillel would rule that [the blood] imparts impurity [whether] moist or dry; and [the reason] that the mishna stated "and she did not immerse" is on account of Beit Shammai. And if you say: But in [tractate] Eduyot [5:4], this [mishna regarding the blood] of a woman who gave birth is taught among the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel — yet in [the case of a woman who is] continuously discharging from within forty [days] (to after forty), Beit Hillel are [ruling] leniently! And one can answer that when [this question] was asked, it was asked regarding the beginning of childbirth [i.e., at the end of the initial days of impurity].

Tosafot on Niddah 35b:25:1.hebrew: אי בשופעת למאי איצטריך - וא"ת: מכל מקום משום בית שמאי איצטריך, כדמשני; ומאי סלקא דעתיה דמקשה, דהא לרב נמי לא אצטריך סיפא אלא לאשמועינן דמודו בית שמאי דמטמא לח ויבש משום דלא ספרה? ויש לומר: דלרב איצטריך לאשמועינן דמודו בית שמאי ביולדת בזוב משום דמעיין אחד הוא; דאי מרישא, הוה אמינא דטעמייהו משום דקסברי ב' מעיינות הן, ואפילו ביולדת בזוב מטהרין, ובית הלל סברי דמעיין אחד הוא, לכך אצטריך סיפא. אלא ללוי, דמוקי רישא בשופעת וסברי ב"ש מעיין אחד הוא, סיפא מאי קא משמע לן:
Tosafot on Niddah 35b:25:1.english: If [dealing with a woman who] continuously discharges, for what purpose was it necessary - And if you say: In any case, it was necessary on account of Beit Shammai, as [the Gemara] answers; and what did the questioner think, for according to Rav as well, the latter clause was only necessary to teach us that Beit Shammai concede that [the blood] imparts impurity moist and dry because she did not count [the seven clean days]? And one can say: According to Rav, [the latter clause] was necessary to teach us that Beit Shammai concede in [the case of] a woman who gives birth as a zava because it is one spring. For if [we learned only] from the first clause, I would have said that their reasoning is because they maintain that they are two springs, and [therefore] even in [the case of] a woman who gives birth as a zava they would declare [the blood] pure, while Beit Hillel maintain that it is one spring; therefore, the latter clause was necessary. But according to Levi, who establishes the first clause [as dealing] with [a woman who] continuously discharges, and Beit Shammai maintain that it is one spring, what does the latter clause teach us?

Tosafot on Niddah 35b:7:1.hebrew: אי אתם מודים בנדה - תימה, מאי קסברי בית הלל דקמייתי מנדה, דפשיטא כדמהדר להו בית שמאי? וי"ל, דמייתי משום דאיתקש לידה לנדה, דכתיב כימי נדת דותה, וכתיב וטמאה שבועים כנדתה:
Tosafot on Niddah 35b:7:1.english: Do you not concede with regard to a menstruating woman - It is puzzling: What did Beit Hillel maintain, that they brought [a proof] from a menstruating woman (niddah), when it is obvious [that the cases differ], as Beit Shammai responded to them? And one can say that they brought [this comparison] because childbirth (leidah) is juxtaposed to a menstruating woman (niddah), as it is written: "As the days of her menstrual infirmity," and it is written: "And she shall be impure two weeks, as in her menstruation."
